conversation:
miguel: Heads-up — Product wants customer-scoped dashboards for next-week demo. They asked for per-customer latency/cost, noisy-neighbor alerts, and an admin view that filters to a single org. Can infra/runtime teams list the minimal signals we need and the data path changes?

alice: +1. UX question: should the console present a single templated Grafana panel (org selector) or real per-org Grafana folders? Templating is easier but leaks query power.

priya: From infra/runtime side: we need these metrics instrumented at the request boundary: org_id, route, model_variant, token_count, queue_depth, and request_duration_ms. Runtime already has org_id in traces but not propagated into prometheus labels.

miguel: Good. Two internal API options: 1) Add org_id label on metrics emitted by workers (low-latency path, high cardinality) 2) Emit org_id as a dimension into a separate multi-tenant metrics pipeline (e.g., kafka -> aggregator) that builds per-org aggregates and writes only aggregated series to Prometheus. Thoughts on tradeoffs?

dana: Security/privacy: we must ensure RBAC + audit logs for any per-org access. Also recommend hashing org_id in metrics where raw IDs are PII. For dashboards used by support, we might allow unhashed but only behind SSO groups.

alice: From product side, prefer templated dashboards with an "impersonate org" switch for internal users. For customers we'd show only their org. Also need an option to pin customers to a "watchlist" for noisy neighbor tracking.

runtime-team: We can add org_id to spans and logs easily. Metrics labels will affect cardinality — adding org_id to high-cardinality metrics like request_duration_histogram could explode series. We can instead add org_id to counters (tokens, requests) and keep histograms aggregated by model+route.

priya: Agreed. Proposal: keep low-cardinality histograms, add per-org counters for tokens and request_rate, and compute p95 latency per-org via tracing sampling + offline aggregation. That reduces Prometheus cardinality while giving accurate noisy-neighbor signals.

miguel: Example PromQL for token rate per org (templated for Grafana):
```
sum(rate(inference_tokens_total{org_hash="$org_hash"}[5m])) by (model)
```
Will we expose org_hash instead of org_id?

dana: Yes use org_hash for dashboard queries. Store org_id -> org_hash mapping in a secure service (access-controlled). Dashboard users see names resolved only if allowed. All access logged.

alice: For noisy neighbor alerts what rules do we want? My wishlist: sudden spike in tokens (>3x baseline), 95th latency above threshold, sustained queue_depth > N for 2m. Alerts should be per-org and send to support + customer success.

priya: Implementation notes: queue_depth is emitted from worker pool exporter, token spikes from token counter. Baseline requires at least 7d of lookback; for new orgs fallback to absolute thresholds. Also consider burst credits so normalizing against reserved capacity.

miguel: Ops concern: dashboards for many orgs = many templated panels but one Grafana instance. If we decide to create per-customer folders, that'll increase admin overhead. Let's keep templated dashboards + perms gating.

runtime-team: We'll add these instrumentation tasks: 1) add org_hash label to token counter and request counter 2) keep histograms without org label 3) emit a sampled trace tag org_hash for p95 estimation 4) add queue_depth per worker with worker->org attribution when possible.

alice: UX flows we need: quick switcher (search org by name/hash), watchlist with email/Slack alert routing, and a "snapshot" export (time window + perm) to send to customers during incidents.

priya: Data retention/cost note: per-org counters at 1s scrape retention 30d will increase TSDB size. We should consider 15s scrape or pre-aggregate to 1m buckets for per-org series. Also compress org_hash label to short tokens.

miguel: Action items:
- runtime-team: open instrumentation PRs for counters/histograms/tracing (ETA Wed)
- infra(priya): design metrics pipeline option (kafka aggregator vs direct labels) and cost model (ETA Thu)
- product(alice): mock console UX for templated dashboards + watchlist (ETA Tue)
- security(dana): org_hash scheme + access control spec (ETA Thu)
- ops: define alert runbook for noisy neighbor escalations (who gets paged)

alice: I'll draft mockups and include a sample "impersonate" permission set.

priya: If infra goes with aggregator we can keep Prometheus cardinality low and also produce aggregated per-org time-series for the console. Will add perf numbers to the doc.

miguel: Great. Can we meet tomorrow 10am to align? I'll send invite.
